clue.text: They will not keep off the grass!

definitions.text: They will not keep off the grass!

parts.words: They will not keep off the grass!
parts.note: a park notice tells walkers to keep off the lawn; the creatures meant here eat it instead of avoiding it

explanation.surface: An exasperated park keeper complains about people trampling the lawn.
explanation.definitionFit: Plant-eating animals graze, so far from avoiding a lawn they make straight for it as food.

clue.text: Not all of the all-purpose cures do cure

indicators.note: Not all of says the answer is only part of the letters in the words that follow

explanation.surface: A sceptic remarks that remedies claiming to treat everything rarely work.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'cures do cure' as the definition, but only 'cure' matches the verb; 'cures do' completes the surface (the all-purpose cures do not all cure) and acts as link words. The letters run from 'the' into 'all-purpose'.
explanation.definitionFit: To cure an illness is to make the patient well again, a synonym.

clue.text: The salesman scoffed about swindle, the rat!

indicators.note: about means the salesman-and-scoffed letters are wrapped around the swindle word

parts.note: REP is short for a sales representative
scoffed means ate greedily
to rob is to swindle or cheat someone

explanation.surface: Someone is indignant at a salesman who gobbled up a con and is a scoundrel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts ROB inside REP+ATE, after its first three letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A rat is a contemptible, untrustworthy person, which is what a scoundrel or wastrel is.

clue.text: Pointless article holding the writer up

indicators.note: holding means the article's letters contain the next piece

parts.note: IT can stand for a thing or article ('that's it')

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word pen is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a pen is the tool that does the writing

explanation.surface: A critic says a useless piece of writing delays its author.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns PEN into NEP, which IT holds: I-NEP-T.
explanation.definitionFit: Something inept is clumsy and ineffective, so it has no point or purpose.

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, written O
pining means wasting away with longing

explanation.surface: A lovesick person daydreams while pining.
explanation.definitionFit: Opining is giving one's view or supposing, close to thinking or fancying something is so.

explanation.surface: A fitness instructor tells someone to pant quickly.
explanation.definitionFit: To breathe a word is to utter or voice it; an express train or delivery is a fast one.

clue.text: Epic story that's in the news again

indicators.note: in says the answer sits inside the words news again

explanation.surface: A long-running tale has made the headlines once more.
explanation.definitionFit: A saga is a long heroic narrative, originally Norse, much like an epic.

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'A woman — one about' (5): A + I (one) + C (about) leaves L and E unaccounted for; likely OCR has lost words (e.g. something giving LACE or LICE), and no scan or search gives the full clue.

clue.text: Being broadcast, it's acted on the teller of the tale

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered widely, so these letters are spread into a new order

explanation.surface: A performance going out on air affects the narrator.
explanation.definitionFit: A storyteller of short amusing incidents is one who relates them, the narrator of the yarn.

clue.text: He's used to dealing with others' capital assets

definitions.text: He's used to dealing with others' capital assets

parts.words: He's used to dealing with others' capital assets
parts.note: capital is read as of the head, so the assets are people's hair rather than their money

explanation.surface: It sounds like a description of a fund manager handling clients' wealth.
explanation.definitionFit: A hairdresser styles the hair on customers' heads, their crowning glory.

clue.text: Extensive map redrawn by the French

indicators.note: redrawn means the map word is drawn again in a different order

parts.note: LE is French for the

explanation.surface: A large chart has been revised by French cartographers.
explanation.definitionFit: Ample means plentiful or large, synonymous with wide-ranging.

indicators.note: into means the first piece goes inside the next

parts.note: to improve is to better something
One is I, and the 's adds S

explanation.surface: Someone is keen on making an off-the-cuff remark even better.
explanation.definitionFit: To ad-lib is to speak or perform without preparation, a synonym.

clue.text: Not in favour of routine-so sorry!

parts.note: con means against, as in pros and cons
trite means stale and commonplace

explanation.surface: Someone apologises for opposing a dull routine.
explanation.definitionFit: Contrite means feeling remorse, deeply apologetic.

indicators.note: may be suggests the word fined could become another word from the same letters

explanation.surface: A drug user could face a penalty in court.
explanation.definitionFit: A fiend can mean an enthusiast or addict, as in a dope fiend.

clue.text: Now is the time to make a donation!

definitions.text: the time to make a donation!

explanation.surface: A charity appeal urges giving immediately.
explanation.definitionFit: Present-day means current or modern; read literally, a present day is an occasion for giving gifts.

parts.note: a book lover's pastime is perusing, and the same word names a town in Berkshire, so 'place' does double duty

explanation.surface: Someone wonders where a book lover would live.
explanation.walkthrough: READING is a large town in Berkshire, west of London.
explanation.definitionFit: A bibliophile spends time perusing books, and the word for that is also a town name.

indicators.note: a strange contraption is an odd construction, so these letters are put together differently

explanation.surface: Someone travels through space in a weird machine.
explanation.definitionFit: An interval is a gap or space between two things or times.

indicators.note: about means the firm word goes round the next piece

parts.note: set means firm or solid, as of jelly
a simple is an old word for a medicinal herb

explanation.surface: A company deals in a basic soft drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'simple' as a noun is an old word for a medicinal plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Sherbet is a sweet cooling fruit drink, or the fizzy powder for one, with no alcohol.

clue.text: This element is filled with sound

parts.note: brims means is full to the top
a tone is a sound

explanation.surface: A chemist notes this substance is full of noise.
explanation.definitionFit: Brimstone is the old name for sulphur, a chemical element.

parts.note: loud-speaker suggests an amplifier, but means a man of ancient legend with a huge voice

explanation.surface: It reads as an antique Greek audio speaker.
explanation.walkthrough: In Homer's Iliad the herald Stentor had a voice as loud as fifty men.
explanation.definitionFit: The Homeric herald was famed for his booming voice, giving us the word stentorian.

clue.text: Note animosity can lead to a break

parts.note: re is the second note of the sol-fa scale
spite is malice or animosity

explanation.surface: Ill will may bring a relationship to a breaking point.
explanation.definitionFit: A respite is a pause or interval of relief.

clue.text: Birds can get into a satellite

indicators.note: get into means the can word goes inside the next piece

parts.note: Mars is a body orbiting the sun, loosely a satellite of it
a tin is a can

explanation.surface: Birds might stow away inside a satellite.
explanation.walkthrough: Mars is a planet, but as a body orbiting the sun the setter calls it a satellite.
explanation.definitionFit: Martins are swallow-like birds such as the house martin.

indicators.note: turning suggests the letters of gateman are turned around into a new order

explanation.surface: A gatekeeper is going red in the face.
explanation.definitionFit: Magenta is a purplish-red colour, close to deep red.

explanation.surface: Someone notes a firmer teacher may also be more pleasant.
explanation.definitionFit: Nice can mean precise or fastidious, so nicer is more exacting; it also means more pleasant.

parts.note: came means approached
L stands for pounds sterling, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: An animal arrived with cash.
explanation.definitionFit: A camel is a humped desert animal, a beast of burden.

indicators.note: for mixing tells the solver the letters of gin's tops are to be stirred into a new order

explanation.surface: A barman reads the instructions on bottle caps for a cocktail.
explanation.definitionFit: A roadside post bearing arrows and place names gives travellers their way.

explanation.surface: A decorator looks at a bare apartment.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain land is level ground; plain also means unadorned, lacking ornament.

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty, taken as many
an eft is a newt

explanation.surface: Many frogs or newts have vanished.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who has gone away has departed, so is no longer there.

clue.text: Mother folk, though it brings censure

parts.note: a dam is an animal's mother
a nation is a people or folk

explanation.surface: A mother's people bring disapproval on her.
explanation.definitionFit: Damnation is condemnation, the strongest disapproval.

parts.note: one o'clock is a typical lunch hour

explanation.surface: A diner finds a midday meal satisfying.
explanation.definitionFit: To atone is to make amends, satisfaction in the sense of compensation for a wrong.

clue.text: Cry out for the old-fashioned record

parts.note: ye is an archaic spelling of the
an LP is a long-playing record

explanation.surface: Someone protests in favour of vinyl records.
explanation.definitionFit: To yelp is to give a sharp, short shout of pain or alarm.

parts.note: re means about or concerning

indicators.note: split means the pollution word is broken open to take the people word

parts.note: taint is contamination
men are people

explanation.surface: A group divided over environmental contamination.
explanation.walkthrough: 'split' puts MEN into TAINT between N and T.
explanation.definitionFit: Retainment is the act of retaining, holding on to something.
